desc: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are an archipelago of over 570 islands in the Bay of Bengal, forming a union territory of India. The islands are divided into the Andaman group to the north and the Nicobar group to the south, separated by the Ten Degree Channel. The archipelago is known for its pristine beaches, coral reefs, and rainforests. The islands are home to several indigenous tribes including the Jarawa, Sentinelese, and Great Andamanese. The capital is Port Blair, and the islands are a popular ecotourism destination. The archipelago is of strategic importance, hosting India's only tri-service military command.
fact: The archipelago has over 570 islands in the Bay of Bengal · It is divided into the Andaman and Nicobar groups separated by the Ten Degree Channel · It is home to several indigenous tribes including the Sentinelese · The islands are a popular ecotourism destination with pristine coral reefs and rainforests

desc: Lakshadweep is an archipelago of 36 islands in the Arabian Sea off the southwestern coast of India, forming the smallest union territory of India. The name means 'one hundred thousand islands' in Sanskrit. Only 10 islands are inhabited, with a total population of about 65,000. The archipelago is known for its pristine coral atolls, turquoise lagoons, and rich marine biodiversity. The islands are protected as a UNESCO-designated biosphere reserve. The capital is Kavaratti, and the primary economy is fishing, coconut cultivation, and tourism. The islands are of strategic importance for India's maritime security.
fact: Lakshadweep is an archipelago of 36 coral atoll islands in the Arabian Sea · Only 10 of the 36 islands are inhabited · The islands are a UNESCO biosphere reserve with pristine coral reefs · The capital is Kavaratti, and the economy is based on fishing, coconut, and tourism

desc: The Maldives is an archipelago nation of 26 coral atolls in the Indian Ocean, comprising about 1,190 islands, of which 200 are inhabited. It is the lowest-lying country in the world with an average ground level of 1.5 meters above sea level. The islands are known for their stunning white-sand beaches, crystal-clear lagoons, and world-class scuba diving. The economy is almost entirely dependent on tourism and fishing. The capital is Malé, one of the most densely populated cities in the world. The Maldives is at the forefront of climate change vulnerability, facing existential threat from sea level rise. The archipelago is home to unique coral reef ecosystems with over 1,000 fish species.
fact: The Maldives is the lowest-lying country in the world at 1.5 meters average elevation · It has 1,190 islands in 26 coral atolls · The capital Malé is one of the most densely populated cities globally · The nation faces existential threat from climate change-induced sea level rise

desc: Seychelles is an archipelago nation of 115 islands in the Indian Ocean, located northeast of Madagascar. It is the least populated sovereign country in Africa with about 100,000 people. The archipelago is famous for its pristine granite and coral islands, white-sand beaches, and unique biodiversity including the giant Aldabra tortoise and the Coco de Mer palm. The capital is Victoria on Mahé Island, the largest island. Seychelles has the highest GDP per capita in Africa, driven by tourism and fishing. The islands have some of the most protected marine areas in the world, with over 50% of the land designated as nature reserves.
fact: Seychelles is an archipelago of 115 islands in the Indian Ocean, the least populated African country · It is home to the giant Aldabra tortoise and the Coco de Mer palm · Over 50% of the land is designated as nature reserves · The capital Victoria is on Mahé, the largest island
